_about.what: All words on web/plain/ (the plain-language front door), English and Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), one {en, zh} pair per field. build-plain.mjs renders index.html from this file and writes copy.js (window.PLAIN_COPY) for the chart labels.
_about.syntax: {id} = a number computed from web/squeeze/data.json by facts.js (rendered as <span data-fact="id">); **text** = the one bold number of a paragraph; [label](href) = a link. Any other digit in a string must be on the build's allowlist with its source.
_about.sources: Merged 2026-09-26 from scratchpad drafts copy-en.json (EN writer), copy-zh.json (繁中 writer, written natively, not translated) and design.md (layout, chart labels, section split).

_merge: Section ids: the drafts used different ids (EN short/token/shelf/cost/restock/why/hakari/see; 繁中 short-version/stock-token/shelf/wild-price/restock/why/hakari/see-it). Both now use the design's anchors: top, token, route, shelf, price, cost, restock, why, hakari, see.

Both drafts had 8 sections; the design has one figure per row, so two draft sections are split. Draft 'shelf' becomes #route (what a pool is + the BONER route) and #shelf (the drain, 2,606 → under 4). Draft 'cost' / 'wild-price' becomes #price (71.23 against 28.84) and #cost (1,351 → 12, 3.85 at the low). The second rows take their headlines from the design ('A memecoin that had to buy HIMS first', 'And moving it became almost free').

Float squeeze vs short squeeze: EN had it in 'why' with @0xSammy's quote, 繁中 in 'wild-price' with the RoaringKitty question. Both now sit in #why with the quote (繁中 gives the English original beside a translation). The RoaringKitty post stays as the X aside in #shelf.

Points one draft had and the other lacked were added to the other language so both tell the same story: the 繁中 Monday recovery line and the EN HAKARI line in the short version; the Friday burns in 繁中 'token'; the reopening at 00:00 and the small arbitrage profits in both 'restock'; DeFiPrime's late buyers and the 30-minute average at the peak in both 'why'; the longest refusal run, the 10,000 USDG caveat (design) and the 00:51 trust in both 'hakari'; the DeFiPrime source for 28.84 in both 'see'.

Units: the EN draft called USDG amounts 'dollars for short'. Amounts are now always written 'USDG' and USDG is defined once as a dollar stablecoin, with no claim that it equals one US dollar; 28.84 is labelled US dollars.

Headlines kept from the drafts; where the two differed in meaning, the 繁中 one was aligned to the EN idea (token, why). The 繁中 '想多知道一點：' prefixes became a shared label. The EN numbers lists and the 繁中 numbers lists are replaced by facts.js: each number is computed from its data key at build time and shown with that key in the page's source table.

Dropped: EN 'about 91% / 9%' split (kept only as 'about 9%', from story.json roles), the EN '1,307 at 09:54' visual-only figure, the 繁中 'about 25-50K USDG' BONER direct-pool size, the draft cta blocks (merged into the four #see cards).

dek.en: One weekend, a token for a stock that closed at {nav} US dollars traded at about {peakRound}. Here is how that happened and why it matters. We also replayed the weekend through HAKARI, a safety check this pool never had.

en: On Friday 28 August 2026, Hims & Hers stock closed at {nav} US dollars in New York. Hims & Hers is a US health company. Two days later, on Sunday night, a token for that same stock traded at about **{peakRound}** on a blockchain. That is about {ratioHalf} times the real price.

Nothing had happened to the company. Over the weekend, no new tokens could be made. Then buyers of a memecoin called BONER took almost all the HIMS out of the main trading pool. With the shelf empty, small purchases pushed the price way up. On Monday new tokens arrived, and about {backMin} minutes later the price was back.
Why does it matter? An app that lends or pays out on this price would have treated each token as worth about {peakRound}. Worse, the price had become almost free to push around on purpose.

HAKARI is a safety check for moments like this. It spots when a price is cheap to fake compared with the money riding on it. Then it refuses to pay out. This pool never had HAKARI. In a replay of the weekend, it would have refused.
zh: 2026 年 8 月最後一個週末，美股 HIMS（Hims & Hers）週五收在 {nav} 美元。可是在 Robinhood 的區塊鏈上，代表這檔股票的代幣，週日深夜一度被報到約 **{peakRound}**。這差不多是收盤價的 {ratioHalf} 倍。
這跟公司本身無關。週末做不出新代幣，偏偏又有一個叫 BONER 的迷因幣，把主要交易池裡的 HIMS 幾乎買光。貨架一空，一點小買單就能把價格推得很高。週一新代幣一到，大約 {backMin} 分鐘，價格就回到原位。
為什麼重要？如果有借貸或結算的應用照這個價格算錢，每顆 HIMS 就會被當成約 {peakRound}。更糟的是，當時要故意把價格推高，幾乎不用花錢。
HAKARI 就是為這種時刻設計的安全檢查：價格很便宜就能造假、押在上面的錢卻很多時，它就拒絕付錢。那個池子當時沒有裝 HAKARI；我們拿真實交易重播一遍，它會拒絕。

unitNote.en: Prices on the blockchain are in USDG, a dollar stablecoin: a token built to track the US dollar. The Friday close of {nav} is in real US dollars. All times are UTC (Taipei is 8 hours ahead, Tokyo 9).
unitNote.zh: 鏈上價格都以 USDG 計；USDG 是一種美元穩定幣，也就是設計來跟著美元走的代幣。週五收盤價 {nav} 是真正的美元。本頁時間都是 UTC（世界標準時間），台灣時間請加 8 小時。

headline.en: A token that stands for a real share
headline.zh: 一顆代幣，對應一股真股票

en: Robinhood, the US trading app, runs its own blockchain called Robinhood Chain. On it, people can hold tokens that stand for shares of real companies. HIMS is the token for one share of Hims & Hers.
zh: Robinhood 是美國的券商 App，自己經營一條區塊鏈，叫 Robinhood Chain。這裡的 HIMS 是「代幣化股票」：Robinhood 在這條鏈上發行的代幣，每一顆對應一股真正的 Hims & Hers 股票。

en: Robinhood makes new tokens backed by real shares it holds. It removes tokens when people cash them in. But it can only do this while its stock trading is open. So from Friday night until the first new tokens on Monday, the number of HIMS tokens was stuck at about **{float}**.
Think of a shop that cannot restock on weekends. If a crowd shows up on Sunday, the shelf can empty. No truck is coming until Monday.
zh: Robinhood 手上有真股票，才會做出對應的新代幣（正式說法：鑄造）。有人把代幣交回去，代幣就收掉（正式說法：贖回）。但這兩件事，只能在 Robinhood 的股票交易時段內做。
所以週末就像倉庫關門的店：架上有多少就是多少，不能補貨，也不能退貨。從週五晚上到週一第一批新代幣出現，鏈上的 HIMS 一直固定在約 **{float}** 顆。

takeaway.en: Over the weekend, no new HIMS tokens could be made. The supply was frozen.
takeaway.zh: 平日缺貨可以補；週末數量是死的，只有約 {float} 顆。

curious.en: Making and cashing in tokens (minting and redeeming) follows Robinhood's round-the-clock weekday hours, called 24/5. This weekend they were shut from Sat 00:00 to Mon 00:00 UTC. On Friday evening, {burned} HIMS were cashed in. That took the count from about {supplyFri} to about {float}. It stayed there until Monday's first new tokens.
curious.zh: 做新代幣和收回代幣，跟著 Robinhood 的「24/5」平日全天交易時段走：紐約時間週日晚上 8 點，到週五晚上 8 點。這個週末關閉的時間，是 UTC 週六 00:00 到週一 00:00。週五晚上有 {burned} 顆被換回，總數從約 {supplyFri} 降到約 {float}，一直停到週一第一批新代幣。

saidPlain.en: A co-founder of a project called LONG said this was not a squeeze on the real stock. No new tokens can be made on weekends, the post said. Once they can, traders will close the gap.
saidPlain.zh: LONG 這個專案的共同創辦人說：這不是真股票被擠壓。週末做不出新代幣；等能做的時候，自然會有人把價差補平。

headline.en: A memecoin that had to buy HIMS first
headline.zh: 一個得先買 HIMS 的迷因幣

en: A memecoin is a joke token that people trade for fun and fast gains. One, called BONER, was priced in HIMS instead of dollars.
zh: BONER 是一個迷因幣，也就是靠話題和社群炒起來的代幣。它有個特別的地方：不是用美元標價，而是用 HIMS 標價。

en: Most people buy HIMS from one main dollar pool: a shared pot of HIMS and USDG that anyone can trade against. The more HIMS people take out, the higher the price of the next one. Think of this pool as the shelf in our shop.

To buy BONER with dollars, you first bought HIMS off that shelf. Then you swapped the HIMS for BONER. That HIMS then sat in BONER's own pool until someone sold BONER. By Monday {bonerMaxTime} UTC, BONER's pool held **{bonerMax}** HIMS, about {bonerShare}% of all HIMS tokens.
zh: 大家用美元買賣 HIMS 的地方，是一個「大家交易用的共同資金池」（流動性池），裡面放著 HIMS 和 USDG，誰都能跟它交易。池子裡的 HIMS 被拿走越多，下一顆就越貴。可以把它想成店裡的貨架。
所以用美元買 BONER，主要路線是先用美元買進 HIMS，再拿 HIMS 去換 BONER。每一筆這樣的買單，都會順手帶走一些 HIMS。這些 HIMS 進了 BONER 的池子，要等有人賣 BONER 才會出來。到週一 {bonerMaxTime}（UTC），BONER 的池子握有 **{bonerMax}** 顆 HIMS，約是全部 HIMS 的 {bonerShare}%。

takeaway.en: People were buying a memecoin, but the stock token is what got carried off.
takeaway.zh: 大家買的是迷因幣，被搬走的卻是股票代幣。

curious.en: BONER also had a smaller pool priced directly in USDG. But its main market was the one priced in HIMS, so most dollar buying went through HIMS first.
curious.zh: BONER 另有一個直接用美元交易的池子，但比較小。它的主要市場是用 HIMS 標價的那個，所以大部分用美元的買單，都得先經過 HIMS。

title.zh: 一塊美元怎麼走到 BONER

caption.en: The route a dollar took to reach BONER. The dollar pool emptied while BONER's pool filled up. BONER's pool also drew HIMS from other pools and wallets, so it grew by more than the dollar pool lost. HIMS's “factory” was closed until Monday, so nothing refilled the dollar pool.
caption.zh: 一塊美元走到 BONER 的路線。美元池被搬空，BONER 的池子越堆越多。BONER 的池子也從其他池子和錢包吸進 HIMS，所以它多出來的，比美元池少掉的還多。HIMS 的「工廠」要到週一才開門，所以沒有東西能補回美元池。

headline.zh: 一個迷因幣，把貨架搬空

en: On Sunday evening, buying of BONER far outweighed selling. At 19:40 UTC, the dollar shelf held about **{pool1940}** HIMS. Fewer than four hours later, at 23:25, fewer than {poolMinUnder} were left.
zh: 週日晚上，BONER 的買盤遠遠大過賣盤。19:40（UTC），美元池這個貨架上還有約 **{pool1940}** 顆 HIMS；不到四小時後的 23:25，只剩不到 {poolMinUnder} 顆。

en: The fall was not steady. At 21:30 about {pool2130} were still there. Half an hour later, at 22:00, only {pool2200}. At 23:25, just **{poolMin}**.
The pool was not short of money: it held {poolUsdgMin} USDG. It was short of HIMS. Think of a shop with a full till and an empty shelf.
zh: 而且不是慢慢變少。21:30 還有約 {pool2130} 顆，半小時後的 22:00 只剩 {pool2200} 顆，23:25 只剩 **{poolMin}** 顆。
池子不缺錢：裡面有 {poolUsdgMin} USDG。它缺的是 HIMS——收銀機滿滿，貨架空空。

takeaway.en: Memecoin buying drained the HIMS shelf, and no restock could come until Monday.
takeaway.zh: 迷因幣的買盤把 HIMS 貨架搬空，而週一之前不可能補貨。

curious.en: Where did the HIMS go? The pool's providers (LPs) had placed it at set prices. As the price rose through them, their HIMS was sold to buyers. Only about 9% of the drop came from providers taking theirs out. At 23:24:59, one purchase bought the last HIMS for sale in the pool. A few HIMS came back within seconds, so at 23:25 the pool held {poolMin}.
curious.zh: HIMS 去哪了？池子的提供者（LP）把貨放在各自設定的價格上。價格一路漲過去，這些 HIMS 就一路賣給買家。提供者自己撤走的，只占減少量的約 9%。23:24:59 那一刻，一筆買單把池子裡能買的 HIMS 全部買光；幾秒內又有幾顆回到池裡，所以 23:25 時是 {poolMin} 顆。

saidPlain.en: An account called RoaringKitty asked if HIMS was being squeezed on Robinhood Chain, pointing at BONER's chart. It is not confirmed to be the famous GameStop trader. Just 13 seconds later, one purchase bought the last HIMS for sale in the dollar pool.
saidPlain.zh: 一個叫 RoaringKitty 的帳號，指著 BONER 的走勢問：HIMS 是不是在 Robinhood Chain 上被軋空了？（未確認是 GameStop 時期那位知名交易員。）13 秒後，一筆買單把美元池裡能買的 HIMS 全部買光。

label.en: Minute by minute: the pool runs dry →

headline.en: An empty shelf makes a wild price

en: A pool's price depends on what is left in it. With almost no HIMS left, each small purchase moved the price a lot. At {peakTime} UTC on Sunday, the price closed that minute at **{peakClose}**. The real stock had closed at {nav}.
zh: 這種池子的定價規則很單純：架上剩越少，價格就喊越高。HIMS 只剩幾顆時，每一筆小買單都能把價格推動很多。{peakTime}（UTC）這一分鐘，池子收在 **{peakClose}**，是週五收盤價 {nav} 的 {ratioHalf} 倍左右。

en: On a normal weekday, new tokens would flow in and pull a wild price back down. This weekend, nobody could make new tokens. So the wild price just stayed.
zh: 平常的日子，新代幣會流進來，把離譜的價格拉回去。這個週末沒有人能做出新代幣，所以離譜的價格就一直掛在那裡。

title.en: You may have seen “$132” on X
title.zh: 你可能在 X 上看過「132 美元」

text.en: That number spread from a news story the next day. In the main pool, nobody bought anywhere near that price. After one small purchase, the pool's price read {peakSwap} for an instant. But that buyer paid about {peakSwapPaidRound} per token on average. One tiny trade, about half a token, did go through at about 133. It was in a small side pool that charged a 50% fee. This page uses the price at the end of each minute. Its highest was {peakClose}.
text.zh: 這個數字，是隔天一篇新聞報導傳開的。主要美元池裡，沒有人用接近這個價格買到。有一筆小買單成交後，池子的報價一瞬間跳到 {peakSwap}；但那筆買單平均每顆只付了約 {peakSwapPaidRound}。確實有一筆約半顆的小交易，以約 133 成交，但那是在一個收 50% 手續費的小池子裡。本頁用每一分鐘結束時的價格，最高是 {peakClose}。

takeaway.en: The blockchain price hit about two and a half times the real one, and nobody could fix it until Monday.
takeaway.zh: 鏈上價格衝到真實股價的約 {ratioHalf} 倍，而週一之前沒有人能把它拉回來。

curious.en: {peakClose} is the pool's price at the end of one minute. It is not a price at which anyone could buy a lot.
curious.zh: {peakClose} 是池子某一分鐘最後的報價，不是能大量買到的價格。

caption.zh: 主要美元池裡一顆 HIMS 代幣的價格（每分鐘結束時），對照真實股票的週五收盤價。灰底：不能做出新代幣的時段。

headline.en: And moving it became almost free
headline.zh: 而且，推動它幾乎不花錢

en: The price also became very cheap to move. Our test: buy enough to push the price up 10%, then sell straight back. You get most of your money back. What you lose is the fees, and that loss is the cost.
zh: 更麻煩的是，價格變得很好推。我們的測法是：買一筆把價格推高 10%，再馬上賣回去。大部分的錢會拿回來，虧掉的是手續費；這筆虧損就是成本。

en: At 19:40 that cost about **{cost1940}** USDG. At 23:25 it cost just {costMin}. At 23:53 it was still only about **{cost2353}**. After Monday's new tokens, it rose again, to {cost0159} by 01:59.
A price that costs almost nothing to move tells you almost nothing. The pool kept showing it anyway.
zh: 19:40 要花約 **{cost1940}** USDG；23:25 只要 {costMin}；到了 23:53，也還只要約 **{cost2353}**。週一新代幣進場後，成本又漲回來，01:59 是 {cost0159}。
一個幾乎不花錢就推得動的價格，幾乎沒有參考價值；但池子照樣一直報出來。

takeaway.en: In about four hours, moving the price 10% became more than 100 times cheaper.
takeaway.zh: 把價格推高 10%，從要花約 {cost1940}，變成只要約 {cost2353}，便宜了一百多倍。

curious.en: HAKARI's measuring tool can check this cost for any pool today. For that weekend, we worked it out minute by minute from the pool's own records. Many providers (LPs) placed the pool's HIMS, each within a price range. Once the price rose past those ranges, almost nothing was left there. So a little money moved it a lot.
curious.zh: HAKARI 的量測工具，現在就能量任何一個池子的這個成本。那個週末的數字，是我們用池子自己的紀錄逐分鐘算出來的。池子裡的貨，由許多流動性提供者（LP）各自放在某個價格區間裡。價格一漲出這些區間，上面幾乎沒貨，一點錢就推得動。

en: On Monday at 00:00 UTC, Robinhood's weekday trading reopened. (It runs day and night on weekdays.) That was 8 pm Sunday in New York. The stock exchange there did not open until {nyseOpen} UTC. {reopenGap} minutes after Robinhood reopened, at {firstMint}, the first new HIMS tokens since Friday arrived: {firstMintAmt} of them. The token maker's own trading wallet then sold them into the pools as they came in.
zh: 週一 00:00（UTC），Robinhood 的平日全天交易時段重新開張。這時紐約還是週日晚上 8 點，紐約證交所要到 UTC {nyseOpen} 才開盤。開張 {reopenGap} 分鐘後，第一批新的 HIMS 在 {firstMint} 上鏈，一次 {firstMintAmt} 顆。Robinhood 發行端自己的交易錢包，新貨一到就賣進池子。

en: The price fell fast. About **{backMin}** minutes after the first new tokens, it was back within 2% of Friday's {nav}. After that, it stayed within 10% of it through Monday {dataEnd} UTC, where our data ends.
By 09:54 UTC, Robinhood had made new tokens in {mints0954} batches. The count grew from about {float} to about **{supply0954}**, more than double.
zh: 溢價很快消失：第一批新貨出現後約 **{backMin}** 分鐘，價格回到週五收盤價 {nav} 的 2% 以內。之後一直到週一 {dataEnd}（UTC，我們資料的終點），都沒有再偏離超過 10%。
到早上 09:54，一共新增了 {mints0954} 批、約 {minted0954} 顆。鏈上的 HIMS 從約 {float} 顆變成約 **{supply0954}** 顆，多了一倍以上。

takeaway.en: Once new tokens could be made, the wild price was gone in about {backMin} minutes.
takeaway.zh: 貨一補上，離譜的價格就沒了。出問題的不是股票，而是週末補不了貨。

curious.en: Between the reopening and the first new tokens, the price spiked again, with a minute close above {close0037} at 00:37. Traders who could not make new tokens had no way to close the gap. Seconds after the first new tokens, two quick round-trip trades made only about {arb1} and {arb2} USDG before costs.
curious.zh: 重新開張到第一批新代幣之間，價格又衝了一次，00:37 那一分鐘收在 {close0037} 以上。不能做新代幣的交易者，沒辦法把價差補平。第一批新貨上鏈後幾秒，兩筆繞一圈的快速交易，扣成本前只賺約 {arb1} 和 {arb2} USDG。

saidPlain.en: This post predicted the gap would close once the token maker could make new tokens and sell them. The maker would profit, it said, and weekend buyers would take the loss. The first new tokens came 58 seconds later.
saidPlain.zh: 這則貼文預言：只要能做新代幣的一方開始做、開始賣，價差就會消失；做代幣的一方賺錢，週末追高的人被套。58 秒後，第一批新代幣就上鏈了。

headline.en: Apps could have paid out on that price
headline.zh: 應用程式可能照這個價格付錢

en: Some blockchain apps read prices straight from pools. Lending apps use the price to value what borrowers put up. Options and perpetual futures, which are bets on where a price goes, use it to decide who gets paid. We are not saying any app read this pool. The cards show what one would have done if it had.
zh: 有些區塊鏈應用會直接讀池子的價格來算錢，例如借貸（拿代幣抵押借錢）、選擇權（押漲跌），還有永續合約（不會到期的期貨）。我們不是說真的有應用讀了這個池子；下面三張卡，是假如有的話，會發生什麼事。

en: On Sunday night, any app reading this pool would have seen HIMS at up to about **{peakRound}**. That was real trading, not a glitch. But it was far from the stock's value. Nobody could correct it until Monday.

Nobody had to cheat for this to happen. One post online called it a short squeeze. That is when traders betting on a fall are forced to buy back. But nobody needed to be betting against HIMS here. As @0xSammy put it on X, [“It’s a float squeeze not a short squeeze.”](https://x.com/0xSammy/status/2094821693747269800) The float is the number of tokens free to trade, and it was stuck.
Who lost? According to DeFiPrime, mostly late buyers. People who bought HIMS at 40 to 60 USDG on Sunday night held a token worth about 29 a few hours later.

Worse, by late Sunday a 10% push cost only about {cost2353} USDG. So someone could push the price up on purpose, then borrow or collect far more than the push cost. That is what faking a price means. It is what HAKARI checks for.
zh: 如果有應用讀的是這個池子，那個週日深夜它會讀到：一檔收盤 {nav} 的股票，值 **{peakRound}**。這是真的成交，不是系統出錯；但它離股票的真實價值很遠。週一之前，沒有人能把它拉回來。

這不需要任何人作弊。網路上有貼文把它說成「軋空」：押股價下跌的人被迫買回。但這裡根本不需要有人押 HIMS 下跌。就像 @0xSammy 在 X 上說的：[「這是流通量擠壓，不是軋空。」（原文：“It’s a float squeeze not a short squeeze”）](https://x.com/0xSammy/status/2094821693747269800)流通量，就是能自由交易的代幣數量；它被卡住了。
誰吃虧了？照 DeFiPrime 的分析，多半是高點追買的人：週日深夜用 40 到 60 USDG 買進，幾小時後只剩約 29。
更危險的是，週日深夜把價格推高 10%，只要約 {cost2353} USDG。有心人可以花小錢故意把價格推高，讓借貸應用多借給他、讓選擇權多賠給他。這就叫價格「造假」，也正是 HAKARI 要防的事。

takeaway.en: A price can come from honest trading and still be unsafe to pay out on.
takeaway.zh: 價格是真的成交出來的，不代表它能拿來付錢。

curious.en: HAKARI calls a pool like this “fenced”. The trading that usually pulls the price back cannot reach it. So a pushed price stays put. Apps often smooth prices with an average over time (a TWAP). That only slows things down. In our replay, the {twapMin}-minute average at {peakTime} was still {twap2331}, more than half above {nav}. This pool never kept an average like that, so the figure is worked out after the fact.
curious.zh: HAKARI 把這種池子叫做「被圍起來的」（fenced）：平常把價格拉回股價的交易進不來，價格被推上去就停在那裡。應用讀價格的管道叫「預言機」（oracle），常用一段時間的平均價（TWAP）來防亂跳，但平均價只是慢一點跟上。我們事後重播推算：{peakTime} 的 {twapMin} 分鐘平均價仍有 {twap2331}，比收盤價 {nav} 高五成多。這是推算，池子當時其實沒裝這種紀錄器。

text.zh: 會把每顆 HIMS 算成 {peakClose}，讓你拿它來借錢。

text.zh: 會當作 HIMS 值 {peakClose} 來結算付款。

text.zh: 會用 {peakClose} 計算手上的部位，賭它會跌的人可能被迫認賠出場。

headline.en: Check the cost of faking before paying out

en: HAKARI is Japanese for a weighing scale. It is a safety check that apps can run before they pay out on a price. It asks: how much would it cost to fake this price right now? From that, it works out a **safe amount**: the most money that can safely depend on the price. A smaller payout goes ahead. A bigger one, HAKARI refuses.
zh: HAKARI 是日文的「秤」。應用要照某個價格付錢之前，可以先問它：現在要把這個價格做假，得花多少錢？它從這個答案算出一個「**安全金額**」，也就是最多能有多少錢押在這個價格上。要付的錢比它少，就照付；比它多，HAKARI 就拒絕。

title.en: A worked example from the replay (this pool never had HAKARI)
title.zh: 重播裡的一個例子（這個池子從未裝上 HAKARI）

text.en: HAKARI tries pushes of several sizes and uses the one that is the best deal for a cheater. At 23:25 on Sunday, that was a push of about {fakeMove}%, costing about **{fakeCost}** USDG. A smaller push costs less, but it also wins less. A price faked {fakeMove}% too high makes every 1 USDG that depends on it pay out {fakeGain} USDG too much. So the safe amount was {fakeCost} ÷ {fakeGain}, about **{safeMin}** USDG.
text.zh: HAKARI 會試好幾種推高的幅度，挑對作弊者最划算的那一種。週日 23:25，最划算的是把價格推高約 {fakeMove}%，只要約 **{fakeCost}** USDG。推得少一點更便宜，但能多拿的錢也更少。價格被假造高了 {fakeMove}%，押在這個價格上的每 1 USDG，就會多付 {fakeGain} USDG。所以安全金額是 {fakeCost} ÷ {fakeGain}，約 **{safeMin}** USDG。

en: **This pool never had HAKARI.** We replayed that weekend's real trades through HAKARI's rules, minute by minute. So this is a what-if replay, not a record. In the replay, the safe amount was about {safe1940} USDG at 19:40 on Sunday. By 23:25, it had fallen to about {safeMinRound}.

So, in the replay, a payout worth 1,000 USDG would have been refused for **{refused}** minutes, about three hours in all. The longest stretch ran two hours, from {runFrom} to {runTo}. Our first version of the rule would have paid out in those minutes, at prices up to {v0Max}. That is nearly 80% above Friday's close. An internal review caught this, and we replaced that version.

The new rule has a limit too. HAKARI checks how cheap a price is to fake. It does not know what the stock is worth. In the replay, new tokens had made the pool deeper again by {trustTime} on Monday. So HAKARI would have let a 1,000 USDG payout through, at its {twapMin}-minute average price of {trust0051}. The pool itself was already down to {pool0051}.

Even on a calm evening, this small pool could safely carry only about {safe1940} USDG in the replay. So a 10,000 USDG payout would have been refused anyway. That is the pool's normal size, not the squeeze.
zh: **先講清楚：那個池子當時沒有裝 HAKARI。**我們是拿它那晚真實的每一筆交易，套上 HAKARI 的規則逐分鐘重跑一遍，所以這是重播推演，不是紀錄。重播中，安全金額從 19:40 的約 {safe1940} USDG，掉到 23:25 只剩約 {safeMinRound} USDG。
換成一筆 1,000 USDG 的結算：在重播中，HAKARI 會拒絕 **{refused}** 分鐘，加起來大約三小時。最長一次從 {runFrom} 到 {runTo}，連續兩小時。我們第一版的規則，在這些分鐘裡會照付，價格最高算到 {v0Max}，比週五收盤價高了將近八成。內部審查抓到這個問題，那一版已經換掉。
新規則也有它的極限。HAKARI 算的是造假有多便宜，不是股票值多少。在重播中，到了週一 {trustTime}，新代幣已經讓池子變深，HAKARI 就會放行一筆 1,000 USDG 的結算。它用的是 {twapMin} 分鐘平均價 {trust0051}，但那時池子本身的價格已經掉到 {pool0051}。
在重播中，即使是平靜的傍晚，這個小池子也只能安全承載約 {safe1940} USDG。所以 10,000 USDG 的結算，本來就會被拒絕。那是它平常的深度，不是擠壓造成的。

takeaway.en: HAKARI says no when faking the price would cost less than a cheater could win from it.
takeaway.zh: HAKARI 不猜價格對不對，只算造假划不划算：造假的成本比能多拿的錢還少，它就拒絕。

curious.en: Of the {refused} refused minutes in the replay, {refusedClosed} came while no new tokens could be made. The other {refusedAfter} came after the first new tokens. The replay assumes nobody trades the price back after a push. That was true while no new tokens could be made. On the weekend of 18 September 2026, we checked 12 stock pools the same way, HIMS among them. None collapsed. (One more pool, MSTR, had no Friday figure to compare.)
curious.zh: 這是重播推演（池子實際沒裝 HAKARI）。{refused} 分鐘的拒絕裡，{refusedClosed} 分鐘在不能做新代幣的期間，{refusedAfter} 分鐘在第一批新代幣之後。重播假設價格被推高後，沒有人把它拉回來；在不能做新代幣的期間，這個假設成立。2026 年 9 月 18 日那個週末，我們用同樣方法檢查了 12 個股票池（包括 HIMS），沒有一個崩掉。（另一個池子 MSTR 沒有週五的數字可比，沒有算進去。）

The Friday close {nav}: [DeFiPrime](https://defiprime.com/tokenized-stock-float-squeeze). X posts: paraphrased from [web/squeeze/social.json](https://github.com/vexi-v1/vexi-hakari/blob/main/web/squeeze/social.json). HAKARI replay: [gauge/data/hims-hook-replay.json](https://github.com/vexi-v1/vexi-hakari/blob/main/gauge/data/hims-hook-replay.json).
sources.zh: 鏈上數字：Robinhood Chain（鏈 ID 4663）的事件紀錄與歷史狀態，重建於 [web/squeeze/data.json](https://github.com/vexi-v1/vexi-hakari/blob/main/web/squeeze/data.json)。週五收盤價 {nav}：[DeFiPrime](https://defiprime.com/tokenized-stock-float-squeeze)。X 貼文：轉述自 [web/squeeze/social.json](https://github.com/vexi-v1/vexi-hakari/blob/main/web/squeeze/social.json)。HAKARI 重播：[gauge/data/hims-hook-replay.json](https://github.com/vexi-v1/vexi-hakari/blob/main/gauge/data/hims-hook-replay.json)。

replay.en: The HIMS/USDG pool never had HAKARI, and it never could. HAKARI has to be built into a pool when the pool is created. Every HAKARI number here comes from running the pool's real trades through HAKARI's rules.
replay.zh: HIMS/USDG 池從未裝上 HAKARI，也不可能裝：HAKARI 必須在池子建立時就裝進去。本頁所有 HAKARI 數字，都是把池子真實的交易套進 HAKARI 規則算出來的。

units.en: USDG is a dollar stablecoin; amounts are in USDG. Prices are the pool's price at the end of each minute. All times UTC.
units.zh: USDG 是一種美元穩定幣；金額單位都是 USDG。價格是池子每一分鐘結束時的價格。時間皆為 UTC。
